title: Drifting and leaving the ground
target: How drifting and being airborne work in R.E.P.O.'s vehicles, so a slide or a jump is something you start on purpose rather than survive.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A ramp or a rise if you want air

steps.do: Know that drifting is a system with its own switch before you look for a button.
steps.because: drifting is a system with its own switch on the vehicle (ItemVehicle, hasDrifting, enableDriftPhysics)

steps.do: Start a drift with speed and angle, not with the handbrake alone.
steps.because: a drift starts from a speed threshold and an angle threshold, and lasts at least a minimum time (driftSpeedThreshold, driftAngleThreshold, driftMinDuration)

steps.do: Expect the slide to slow you down unless you hold it.
steps.because: it has its own turning speed and speed bounds (driftTurningSpeed, driftMaxSpeed, driftMinSpeedRatio)

steps.do: Feed the slide in rather than snapping into it.
steps.because: the speed ramps up over a time when a drift starts (driftSpeedRampUpTime)

steps.do: Use the exit boost deliberately, because leaving a drift changes the drag.
steps.because: leaving a drift applies an exit boost and switches between a drift drag, a default drag and a smoothing time (driftExitBoost, driftDrag, driftDragDefault, driftDragSmoothTime)

steps.do: Watch for the drift's own effects, which change with how hard you are drifting.
steps.because: drifting has particles with a transform, and a light with settings per drift level (driftingParticlesTransform, driftParticles, driftLight, driftLightSettings, driftLevelSettings)

steps.do: Know that being airborne is a system too, with lift of its own.
steps.because: being airborne is a system with its own switch and a lift force (enableAirbornePhysics, airborneLiftForce)

steps.do: Pitch the vehicle in the air and steer less, because the air has its own rules.
steps.because: the vehicle pitches in the air towards a target angle at a speed and strength blended in over a blend speed, steering in the air uses a multiplier of its own, and falling applies a gravity of its own with a maximum and a speed below which it does not apply (airborneTargetPitch, airbornePitchSpeed, airbornePitchStrength, airborneBlendSpeed, airborneSteeringMultiplier, fallGravityAcceleration, fallGravityMax, fallGravityMinDownwardVelocity, fallGravityTopSpeed)

commonMistakes: Expecting a drift to hold itself once it starts.
Snapping into a slide and losing the speed the drift needed.
Steering as hard in the air as on the ground.
Forgetting that falling has its own gravity and a floor to it.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
